item.title: C++ Thread Safety, Reinventing The Wheel, and Making My Life Easier
item.description:
Alternative title: Carcinization? In my C++ codebase? It’s more likely than you think.

Whilst the job search continues, I thought I’d get out a quicker writeup about a lifesaver of a tool I’ve recently implemented in my ongoing project indy-tui1 and how I stumbled iterated my way to it.

Background#

By its nature, indy-tui requires keeping several threads up and running – when managing an interface, user input, and a live websocket session, one’s hand is slightly forced. Likewise, some amount of shared data across threads is largely unavoidable. Hence, it’s time for locking.

item.title: Delayable Telemetry Queue | Design Notes - indy-tui
item.description:
As the core impetus for my most recent (and ongoing) project, I think a break down of my design and implementation of the delay queue used in #indy-tui is perfectly befitting of a first post.

I’ll start with a little background on the project, follwed by a little more on the problem I was trying to solve and why I’m/ taking a crack at it. Then, I’ll touch on the two main approaches I considered, what primary goals I was trying to meet, and ultimately which of the approaches stuck. Finally, I’ll go a little more technically in-depth on the implementation I have today.
